records.question: Should Roulet 12 and 13 have a federal EIA record yet?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists no planned Oklahoma units at Anadarko plant 3006. The Oklahoma permit memorandum and trade press do describe the two turbines.
records.recommendation: Leave both units as construction and recheck the next EIA monthly table due November 24, 2026.
records.researcher_notes: I read the Southwest Power Pool open queue list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). Entry GEN-2023-GR1 is a replacement request of 97.488 MW of gas at the Anadarko 69 kV plant connection, owned by the cooperative, with commercial operation shown as December 2025 and a cessation date of November 2025. Its size fits the two new 50.2 MW turbines, so it is not a third project. Its dates are earlier than the late 2026 completion reported in the press, and I found no report that the turbines are running. Entries GEN-2007-052 at 150 MW and GEN-2005-022 at 177 MW are older plants already in commercial operation and match existing units.

records.question: Is the blank owner in the task right, since the database shows Associated Electric?
records.finding: The database already shows Associated Electric Cooperative Inc at 100 percent. The Associated page at https://www.aeci.org/bristow-energy-center-1 says the cooperative is building the plant, and the Siemens story at https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/stories/gas-turbine-peaker-oklahoma-us.html calls it Associated's plant.
records.recommendation: Leave the owner as it is. Leave the operator blank until a document names one.
records.researcher_notes: No project company was found.

records.question: Is SPP queue row GEN-2024-340 a different project from Bristow?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists GEN-2024-340 as 1,440 MW in Creek County for American Electric Power at the Riverside to Redbud line. That does not match a 420 MW Associated plant.
records.recommendation: Treat it as another project. No queue row for Bristow was found.
records.researcher_notes: Associated may have a queue row under another county or name. The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality harvest found no air permit application for Bristow either. The permit records before 2016 are not online.

records.question: Is GEM's point for Bristow close to the site Associated describes?
records.finding: The Associated page at https://www.aeci.org/bristow-energy-center-1 puts the plant about 2 miles southeast of Bristow. GEM's point at 35.81000, -96.36600 is consistent with that. No address, parcel or coordinates were found.
records.recommendation: Leave the point and the approximate accuracy as they are.
records.researcher_notes: No imagery check was done because no document gave a more exact place. An air permit application would give coordinates.

records.question: Which point is the Citadel data center site, GEM's or the permit's?
records.finding: The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit memo at https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/deq/documents/air-quality/Citadel%20Facility-2026-0286-C.pdf gives latitude 36.27133 and longitude -95.90837. The same memo says the site is at North Yale Avenue and East 86th Street North in Sperry, which geocodes to 36.27857, -95.91994, about 100 meters from GEM's point of 36.27924, -95.91897. The permit point is about 1.3 kilometers from GEM's point.
records.recommendation: Leave the point and the approximate accuracy as they are. Ask the permit engineer or check a county parcel map for the Yale and 86th Street site before making it exact.
records.plant_name: Citadel Facility Data Center power station
records.researcher_notes: Satellite images show ground with no data center built at either place, and the imagery date is unknown. The permit directions start from Owasso and fit the permit point better than the street address. Pin links: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.27133,-95.90837 and https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.27924,-95.91897

records.question: Should the 10 smaller backup engines at Citadel be added as a unit?
records.finding: The permit at https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/deq/documents/air-quality/Citadel%20Facility-2026-0286-C.pdf lists 6 engines of 2,584 horsepower and 4 engines of 1,340 horsepower besides the 108 engines in the two units, plus one fire pump. At about 1.75 MW for the first six, the groups sum to about 10.5 MW and about 5 MW.
records.recommendation: Leave them out. They sum well under the 50 MW bar.
records.plant_name: Citadel Facility Data Center power station
records.researcher_notes: This matches the existing database note from November 4, 2026.

records.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to Comanche CC2 and CC3?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 2G1 at 408.8 MW and 2S1 at 277.6 MW with unit code CC2. It lists generators 3G1 at 408.8 MW and 3S1 at 277.6 MW with unit code CC3. Each pair is a gas turbine plus a steam turbine, so each pair is one combined cycle block.
records.recommendation: Treat 2G1 and 2S1 as CC2, and 3G1 and 3S1 as CC3. Type these ids into Other IDs for the unit by hand in the web form.
records.researcher_notes: EIA's own unit code column names the blocks, so there is no doubt about the pairing. The generators are planned for September 2029 and EIA says regulatory approvals are not initiated, which is out of date because the air permit application was filed in April 2026.

records.question: What capacity should each new Comanche block carry?
records.finding: GEM and the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx show 686.4 MW per block. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows 775.2 MW for each of the two queue entries ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026. The air permit application at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true says each block will produce 633 MW.
records.recommendation: Leave 686.4 MW, which is EIA's nameplate figure. Ask the project manager whether the larger queue figure should be used because it may include duct burner output.
records.researcher_notes: The queue figure may be the interconnection request and not the nameplate. The permit figure is a total output at one set of site conditions. I did not find a document that gives the nameplate in plain terms.

records.question: What capacity should each new Comanche block carry?
records.finding: GEM and the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx show 686.4 MW per block. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows 775.2 MW for each of the two queue entries ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026. The air permit application at https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ATdpa%C3%81tiBf6AUlxodMaTf4RyyKtRvO65cbkkb3aVZbN4JAjNn88hU2pksW3d3Ngw9ZE27%C3%81UOLoThr916JdkRs9c%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true says each block will produce 633 MW.
records.recommendation: Leave 686.4 MW, which is EIA's nameplate figure. Ask the project manager whether the larger queue figure should be used because it may include duct burner output.
records.researcher_notes: The queue figure may be the interconnection request and not the nameplate. The permit figure is a total output at one set of site conditions. I did not find a document that gives the nameplate in plain terms.

records.question: Is SPP queue entry GEN-2024-321 the Cross Timbers plant?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists GEN-2024-321 as a 507 MW gas project in Seminole County, connecting at the Seminole 345 kV substation, with an OG&E owner label and a 2029 in service date. The Cross Timbers permit memorandum at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf describes two turbines of up to 255 MW each at Section 36, Township 6N, Range 5E near Konawa. Two times 255 MW is 510 MW, close to 507 MW.
records.recommendation: Do not add a new unit for GEN-2024-321 now. Leave the queue entry linked to the Seminole station, and ask the project manager to check the queue study documents to see whether OG&E is buying Cross Timbers output.
records.researcher_notes: Nothing I found ties Cross Timbers Power LLC to the queue entry. The queue names OG&E and a substation at the Seminole plant. A web search found no news about Cross Timbers Power. The point of interconnection is the main reason I think it is a different project.

records.question: Should the Cross Timbers point move about 500 meters?
records.finding: GEM's point is 34.95195, -96.73905 and is marked exact. The permit memorandum at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9156.pdf gives 34.95595, -96.73635 for the facility.
records.recommendation: Leave the point as it is. The two points are about 500 meters apart and GEM's is already exact.
records.researcher_notes: I did not open a satellite image. The difference is small compared with the size of the site.

records.question: Should units 11 and 12 stay operating when EIA still shows testing?
records.finding: OG&E said in September 2026 that unit 11 passed its tests and would enter service in October. The October 28, 2026 earnings call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ describes both units as added capacity. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx still shows both as construction complete, not yet in commercial operation, planned October 2026.
records.recommendation: Leave both units as operating. Check the OG&E ribbon cutting release in November 2026 for the exact date.
records.researcher_notes: I did not find a document that gives the commercial operation date. Sierra Club data also shows construction, but it is not cited.

records.question: Which EIA generator ids belong to units 13 and 14?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists generators 13 and 14, each 224 MW, planned February 2029. The earnings call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ gives 440 MW for both, which is 220 MW each.
records.recommendation: Treat EIA generator 13 as unit 13 and generator 14 as unit 14. Both are 224 MW in EIA and in GEM, so no capacity change.
records.researcher_notes: OG&E's own figure of 440 MW total is a rounded plant total.

records.question: How do SPP queue dates ERAS-2025-010 and GEN-2024-GR1 fit units 13 and 14?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists ERAS-2025-010, a 496 MW combustion turbine at the Horseshoe Lake substation with an in-service date of April 2028, and GEN-2024-GR1, 492 MW. OG&E and EIA say units 13 and 14 start in 2029.
records.recommendation: Leave the start year at 2029. The queue entries are about 496 MW, close to two 224 MW units plus margin.
records.researcher_notes: I did not open the 2025 commission docket orders to check for an earlier date, because the call summary and EIA both say 2029 or later.

records.question: Is unit 15 a 2031 start, or is queue entry ERAS-2025-004 for 2029 the same project?
records.finding: The October 28, 2026 call at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-oge-energy-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-28/ says unit 15 is 755 MW and enters service in 2031. The Southwest Power Pool queue at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists ERAS-2025-004, a 756.2 MW combined cycle at the same substation dated April 2029.
records.recommendation: Keep 2031 from the owner's statement and treat the queue entry as the same project with an earlier placeholder date.
records.researcher_notes: The queue is a lead only.

records.question: Is the Energy and Policy Institute proposed record for Horseshoe Lake wrong for unit 10?
records.finding: The Energy and Policy Institute Oil and Gas Watch record at https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/rec_d4f1u5oq7easr8ra1f60 lists the plant as proposed. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists unit 10 as operating, 60.5 MW, started 2001.
records.recommendation: Leave unit 10 as operating. The proposed label most likely reflects the new units 13 to 15.
records.researcher_notes: The record page is drawn by script and its text could not be read by the page checker.

records.question: Is there a document that states Backup Power for the Horseshoe Lake units?
records.finding: I found no document that says whether any Horseshoe Lake unit is a backup power unit. All sources describe the units as grid supply for OG&E customers.
records.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no on all ten units and leave the source box empty.
records.researcher_notes: Searched the 2026 OG&E plan, the September 2026 news release and EIA-860M. None uses the term.

records.question: Where do units 6 and ST7 stand in GEM, and what is their source?
records.finding: Both are retired in GEM with 2024 retirement years. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists unit 6 retired January 2024 and ST7 retired December 2024.
records.recommendation: Leave both as retired, and use the EIA-860M table as the source of the retirement year.
records.researcher_notes: The September 2024 notes in the status detail say to be retired and were not changed.

records.question: Should Site B be 372 MW as in the Southwest Power Pool queue, not 342 MW?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue entry GEN-2024-323 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive) lists 372 MW for the Hugo project at the ITC Hugo 7 345 kV substation. The database has 342 MW from six SGT-800 turbines. A Construction Review article (https://constructionreviewonline.com/1b-hugo-plant-expansion-western-farmers-electric-breaks-ground-on-nine-gas-turbines-in-oklahoma/) says the nine turbines add about 400 MW, and a cooperative annual report says 404 MW.
records.recommendation: Leave 342 MW as it is, since queue sizes often include extra margin. The total of 415.5 MW for both sites is close to the 404 MW to 415 MW reported.
records.researcher_notes: I read the Southwest Power Pool open queue list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). Entry GEN-2024-323 shows a nameplate of 372 MW and a capacity of 356.8 MW, with commercial operation in May 2029. Site A is 73.5 MW in the database and entry GEN-2026-SR34 shows 75 MW, owned by the cooperative, at the Hugo 138 kV substation, with commercial operation in April 2029.

records.question: Should the City for Hugo be Fort Towson, not Fort Townsend?
records.finding: The Rural Utilities Service environmental assessment (https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/rus-ea-hugo-new-generation.pdf) places the site west of Fort Towson, Oklahoma. The database spells it Fort Townsend.
records.recommendation: Change City to Fort Towson for both units. The pin link is https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=34.01875,-95.32186.
records.researcher_notes: Both units are shown as exact in the database, so the coordinates were not reopened.

records.question: Should capacity be 324 MW, summed from the newest draft permit?
records.finding: The database shows 283.1 MW from the earlier fleet of 102 engines. The September 2026 draft permit (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Ae6Ctfv7oSCmhMZ%C3%89kDp%C3%89JKeyyrF%C3%897NeqHWN6Fd0wYTdl604KTTG6bsIhnFC9Sgq7vhd656jR%C3%895uQBkEpWYOBnMg%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true) lists 105 engines, with the MTU units now at 3,250 kW each. My sum of the permit ratings is about 324 MW.
records.recommendation: Change Capacity to 324.0 once the permit is final, or now if you accept a sum of the draft's ratings. The earlier figure used 3.49 MW per MTU engine, which is the engine rating, not the generator rating.
records.researcher_notes: I read the Southwest Power Pool open queue list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). Entry GEN-2025-SR9 is 400 MW with no fuel shown, owned by OG&E, at the Muskogee 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in December 2029. Entry GEN-2024-293 is 248 MW of gas at the same substation name, with commercial operation in May 2033. Both are grid interconnection requests with no site address, and neither names this data center. They are added as separate projects, not as this plant's backup fleet. The permit has not been issued yet, so numbers could still change.

records.question: Should Units 5 and 6 be 229 MW each instead of 225 MW?
records.finding: The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality draft permit memo from September 2026 (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/AWtoGCCMAPa3ZmzV9bv2lNVdjzgKUd4GV4oRCuMNP0goK6NykmHJHyG5WSO1mUZe7mM1J5HwOpKpJWodbQLKNmw%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true) lists two 229 MW GE turbines. The permit application from late 2025 said 222 MW each. The AEP report says 450 MW in total.
records.recommendation: Leave 225 MW on both units, since 450 MW in total matches the AEP report. Change to 229 only if you prefer the permit figure.
records.researcher_notes: The Southwest Power Pool entry ERAS-2025-023 at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive is a single combustion turbine of 513 MW nameplate and 510 MW capacity at the Northeastern 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in December 2029 in the open list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, read on 5 November 2026. It does not match two 229 MW turbines due by the end of 2028. The same Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit file also describes a separate large turbine of nominal 453 MW at Northeastern (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/AS0IjaCrV1T%C3%81SEUDdXmwkZpG2VRBClzAKR911pep%C3%81uAtGhYCcgV7UJnH1xPqDg4ZbOaSJTShXSL302lcWYvl9ds%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true). The permit and the AEP report describe two turbines for Units 5 and 6.

records.question: Should the Oil and Gas Watch and Sierra Club entries for Unit 3 be updated to operating?
records.finding: The AEP report for June 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4904/000000490426000059/aep-20260630.htm) says Unit 3 has run on natural gas since January 2026.
records.recommendation: Keep Unit 3 as operating in GEM. Tell the owners of the Oil and Gas Watch and Sierra Club lists that their proposed and planned labels look out of date.
records.researcher_notes: I could not read the Oil and Gas Watch page, so I did not see its own source documents.

records.question: Is the SPP queue entry ERAS-2025-023 a separate project from Units 5 and 6?
records.finding: The 513 MW queue entry is one turbine with commercial operation in December 2029, a year after the two 229 MW turbines of Units 5 and 6. The queue list names no developer, and no document I found ties it to either project.
records.recommendation: Add no new unit now. Check the Southwest Power Pool list again in the next monthly update and the Oklahoma Corporation Commission docket for a third Northeastern turbine.
records.researcher_notes: An Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit file for Northeastern also describes a separate 453 MW turbine (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/AS0IjaCrV1T%C3%81SEUDdXmwkZpG2VRBClzAKR911pep%C3%81uAtGhYCcgV7UJnH1xPqDg4ZbOaSJTShXSL302lcWYvl9ds%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true). The entry may be that turbine or a later one. I could not tell which from a document.

records.question: Where is the ONE Nuclear Oklahoma gas site?
records.finding: The filing at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1846416/000149315225019001/ex99-1.htm names Oklahoma only. No ODEQ permit, commission cause or queue entry matched, and the point GEM shows could not be checked.
records.recommendation: Leave the point and the blank city as they are. Search again when ONE Nuclear files an air permit or names a county.
records.researcher_notes: The location ladder found no address, so no imagery was checked.

records.question: Is the PSO 2026 resource plan line for Port of Inola still to be found?
records.finding: The commission cause search (the daily docket PDFs) and the queue file matched nothing for this plant. The permit application is the only document found for the 2030 start.
records.recommendation: Ask the reviewer to check PSO's 2026 resource plan refresh by hand for the Port of Inola line and the Oklahoma Corporation Commission cause number.
records.researcher_notes: A web search found no news article naming a combined cycle plant at the Port of Inola.

records.question: Does pre-construction fit Project Thunderbird before any air permit exists?
records.finding: No air permit application, commission filing or queue entry was found. The only documents are news reports of a rezoning request that was delayed in September 2026 (https://okcfox.com/news/local/project-thunderbird-data-center-proposal-promises-600-jobs-and-self-generated-power).
records.recommendation: Change status to announced unless a permit application or land purchase is found. Ask the reviewer to check the Garfield County and Enid records.
records.plant_name: Project Thunderbird Data Center power station
records.researcher_notes: The ODEQ permit harvest matched nothing. An air permit may have been requested under a different name.

records.question: Should Ripley RP1 capacity change from 445 MW to 419 MW?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 419.0 MW nameplate and 444.5 MW net winter. The state permit memorandum (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8877.pdf) gives a nominal gross output of 420 MW.
records.recommendation: Change capacity to 419 MW, the nameplate figure, because the manual wants nameplate and not winter capability.
records.researcher_notes: The old Associated Electric Cooperative page could not be read, so I could not see why 445 was used. It likely came from the winter figure. A second check of the plan found: GEM gives 445 MW, under construction for 2027. The federal file for September 2026 gives 419 MW, under construction, more than half complete. Look for the cooperative's own figure before changing GEM. Keep 445 MW until a document names the nameplate.

verifications.note: Plant 67262 Ripley Energy Center RP1, 419 MW, planned 2027, under construction more than half complete.

records.question: Should the city for Seminole (OK) power station read Konawa instead of Konowa?
records.finding: The 2026 OG&E integrated resource plan at https://ogeenergy.gcs-web.com/static-files/80b39a4f-b2b2-45cc-b848-efc9ba018dd8 places the plant in Konawa, Oklahoma. The tracker shows Konowa.
records.recommendation: Change City to Konawa on every unit of this plant.
records.researcher_notes: An Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit memo for the Seminole Generating Station at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8353.pdf also gives the facility location as Konawa, Seminole County. Two sources agree on this spelling. I found no document that uses Konowa.

records.question: Is the 507 MW gas queue entry GEN-2024-321 a new unit at Seminole?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue page at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive lists GEN-2024-321 as a 507 MW gas project, queued March 2025, with a planned in-service date of March 2029 and a connection at the Seminole 345 kV substation. Two smaller entries, GEN-2025-SR10 at 238 MW and GEN-2025-SR13 at 125 MW, connect at the Seminole 345 kV and 138 kV substations with no fuel shown.
records.recommendation: Ask the project manager whether these are expansions at the OG&E plant or separate projects near the substation. If at the plant, add a new announced unit for GEN-2024-321.
records.researcher_notes: A connection point at a substation does not prove the project sits at the plant site. The queue page gives no developer name or site address that I could read, and the 2026 OG&E plan names no new unit at Seminole. I did not find an air permit for a new unit at Seminole in the harvested permit file.

records.question: Should unit 4 capacity stay at 426 MW or change to 594 MW?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 594.0 MW nameplate for generator 4, and the Southwest Power Pool queue entry GEN-2024-GR5 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive) lists 594 MW as a gas and storage hybrid. The owner's dedication article (https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/grand-river-dam-authority-formally-dedicates-unit-4-grand-river-energy-center) says 426 MW. A 2024 permit memo (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8824.pdf) lists a 453 MW turbine.
records.recommendation: Leave 426 MW for now. If the generator nameplate is 594 MW, change it to 594.
records.researcher_notes: The three numbers describe different ratings. Queue entry GEN-2024-GR5 is a replacement request, with a cessation date of 16 September 2026 and a summer rating of 554 MW against a winter rating of 594 MW in the open list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, read on 5 November 2026. That points to ratings that change with the season, not to extra storage capacity. A rating of 594 MW is a winter figure.

records.question: Which older unit did unit 3 replace?
records.finding: A Black and Veatch project page (https://www.bv.com/projects/power-plant-replacement-project-brings-price-certainties-cleaner-air) names the project Grand River Energy Center Units 2 and 3, which suggests the combined cycle replaced older unit 2. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 still lists a coal unit 2 as operating at 594 MW.
records.recommendation: Find the GEM unit ID of the coal unit 2 at this plant and, if it exists, put it in the replacement link for unit 3. If no unit 2 record exists, ask the project manager whether to add one.
records.researcher_notes: I could not read the GEM unit ID for unit 2 from the brief. I did not find a document that says plainly which unit unit 3 replaced.

records.question: Is Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2025-SR19 at the Maid 161 kV substation part of the Grand River Energy Center?
records.finding: The request is for 100 MW, owned by the Grand River Dam Authority, with no fuel shown, near Chouteau, with commercial operation in November 2029 in the open list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV, read on 5 November 2026. The Grand River Energy Center connects at its own 345 kV substation, which is a different connection point.
records.recommendation: Keep GEN-2025-SR19 as its own new project and add no unit at the Grand River Energy Center.
records.researcher_notes: The queue list gives no site address or project name for this request. I found no air permit or board document that places it at the Grand River Energy Center.

records.question: Is there a document that states Backup Power for the Green Country units?
records.finding: The EIA table and the news article do not state a Backup Power value. The plant sells to the grid.
records.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no and add the EIA table for September 2026 as its source if a source is required.
records.researcher_notes: I did not search the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality air permit files for Green Country beyond the harvested index, which holds a water discharge permit renewal and a 2003 major source permit, neither of which states backup use.

records.question: Is there a document that states Backup Power for the Kiamichi units?
records.finding: The EIA table and the Tenaska fact sheet do not state a Backup Power value. The plant sells power into the grid.
records.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no.
records.researcher_notes: A Title V air permit renewal, number 2026-0277-ARR4, is under review at the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality. I did not open its documents for this check.

records.question: Do the two Southwest Power Pool queue entries at McClain describe new units?

records.question: Is GEN-2016-047, a 24 MW combustion turbine in service since December 2017 at the Mustang 69 kV substation, a unit GEM is missing?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue lists GEN-2016-047 as a 24 MW combustion turbine in service in December 2017 at Mustang 69 kV. The EIA table lists no unit of 24 MW at Mustang. The other Mustang queue entry, GEN-2025-SR23, is now staged as its own new plant, so it is not part of this question.
records.recommendation: Leave GEM as is. Ask OG&E whether the 24 MW turbine is one of the existing Mustang units under a different rating, and add it as a new unit if it is not.

records.question: Is Southwest Power Pool entry ERAS-2025-003 at Redbud a new unit or the turbine upgrade?
records.finding: The Southwest Power Pool entry ERAS-2025-003 lists a 186 MW combined cycle addition at the Redbud 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in January 2027. A state air permit memorandum (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9021.pdf) says the four existing combustion turbines are being upgraded, which raises the plant from about 1,268 MW to 1,490 MW. The 2026 OG&E resource plan (https://ogeenergy.gcs-web.com/static-files/80b39a4f-b2b2-45cc-b848-efc9ba018dd8) lists no new unit at Redbud.
records.recommendation: Do not add a new unit. Treat the entry as the capacity increase of the four existing units, and consider raising each unit from 358 MW to about 372.5 MW once the upgrade is confirmed complete.
records.researcher_notes: I read the OG&E 2026 resource plan. Its list of planned additions names only Horseshoe Lake and Tinker, and its footnote says OG&E owns 51 percent of Redbud, which matches the shares in the database. I read the queue entry in the Southwest Power Pool open list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). It names OG&E as the owner and gives no turbine count. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) shows no planned generator at this plant. I did not find the other owners' shares in a document beyond the database values, so those stay as they are. A second check of the plan found: The SPP queue lists a 186 MW combined cycle request at the Redbud 345 kilovolt substation near Luther with a fully executed agreement, an in-service date of October 24, 2025 and commercial operation on January 18, 2027. GEM has four Redbud units of 358 MW, all operating. Ask OG&E whether this is a combined cycle uprate, and if it is add a note to the Redbud record without a new unit, otherwise add a 186 MW unit with start year 2027.

verifications.note: SPP active queue list updated November 3, 2026. Row ERAS-2025-003.

records.question: Should each Redbud unit's capacity move from 358 MW to 372.5 MW after the upgrade?
records.finding: The permit memorandum (https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/9021.pdf) says each combined cycle unit goes from 317 MW to 372.5 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) still shows 198.9 MW plus 159.5 MW, or 358.4 MW, per unit.
records.recommendation: Leave 358 MW for now. Change all four units to 372.5 MW when EIA or the owner confirms the upgrade is finished.
records.researcher_notes: The memorandum describes planned work, so it does not prove the upgrade is done.

records.question: Were the Oklahoma resource plans and queue entry GEN-2024-255 checked for Spring Creek?
records.finding: I did not open the Evergy resource plan or the Southwest Power Pool entry GEN-2024-255. The brief calls that entry a lead that is not this plant.
records.recommendation: Leave the plant as it is. Check the Evergy plan for a retirement year if a person wants it done.
records.researcher_notes: The 12 fetch budget went to the monthly EIA table only, which covers status and capacity for all four units.

records.question: Is Southwest Power Pool entry ASGI-2014-014 Ferguson the same as this plant?
records.finding: The queue entry shows 56.4 MW, Payne County, a fully executed agreement and commercial operation. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists Stillwater Energy Center with three engines of 18.8 MW each, which sum to 56.4 MW, in service since July 2016.
records.recommendation: Treat the queue entry as this plant and add no new unit. Leave the unit as it is.
records.researcher_notes: The queue page is https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive. It names the entry but does not name the plant, so the match rests on matching capacity and county.

records.question: Is EIA plant 63628 Tinker the same site as this plant?

Generators 1 and 2 (48.1 MW each, operating since March 2026) match unit 1-2. Generators 5A and 5B (41 MW each, out of service, since 1971) match unit 5A-5B.
records.recommendation: Type EIA 63628 into Other IDs (location). Type EIA 1 and EIA 2 into Other IDs (unit) for unit 1-2, and EIA 5A and EIA 5B for unit 5A-5B.

records.researcher_notes: Retired unit 3 (95 MW, retired 2012) is also in EIA and before 2020.

records.finding: The Chickasha Economic Development Authority release page (https://chickashaedc.com/2025/06/governor-stitt-chickasha-leaders-celebrate-largest-private-investment-in-city-history-with-announcement-of-new-industrial-park) carries the note that the project was cancelled as of early 2026 due to site limitations. records.question: Should GEM raise the Muskogee Data Center power station from 283.1 megawatts to about 314 megawatts?
records.finding: Core Scientific's July 2026 permit application asks for 105 diesel generators: 50 of 2.75 or 3 megawatts and one of 1 megawatt at MSK1-A, and 54 of 3.25 megawatts at MSK1-B. That sums to 314.0 megawatts with the 2.75 megawatt model, or 326.5 megawatts with the 3 megawatt model. GEM lists 283.1 megawatts, built from the earlier permit of 102 engines.
records.recommendation: Update the plant to the 105 engines in the July 2026 application once the department issues the modified permit, and use 314.0 megawatts until the engine model is chosen.
records.researcher_notes: The application also renames the buildings MSK1 and MSK2 as MSK1-A and MSK1-B. It changes the 50 engines at the second building to 3.25 megawatt models, adds four more, and drops the house generator there. The old total of 102 engines had 100 main generators and 2 house generators.

verifications.note: Permit application of July 2026 for Core Scientific MSK1-A and MSK1-B in Muskogee. Table 1 lists 50 main generators of 2.75 megawatts or 3 megawatts and one 1 megawatt house generator at MSK1-A, and 54 generators of 3.25 megawatts at MSK1-B.

records.plant_name: Citadel Facility Data Center power station
records.question: Should GEM add the 10 smaller backup engines in the Citadel Facility permit to its 297 megawatt record?
records.finding: The department's comment document for permit 2026-0286-C lists 36 engines of 3,997 horsepower and 72 of 4,043 horsepower, which are the 108 engines GEM counts at 297 megawatts. records.plant_name: Fort James Muskogee Mill Power Plant
records.question: Are the Georgia-Pacific gas steam turbines in the federal file the same units as GEM's Fort James Muskogee Mill coal units 2 and 3?
records.finding: GEM lists Fort James units 2 and 3 at 45.5 MW each, coal, started 1979 and 1982, retired in 2020, with a note about conversion to gas. The federal file for September 2026 lists three operating natural gas steam turbines at the same mill of 25, 44.5 and 44.5 MW from 1979, 1980 and 1982.
records.recommendation: Check the mill's air permit to see whether the turbines are the same. If they are, update the Fort James units to operating on gas and drop the new plant, and if not, keep the new plant and add a Notes line on both.
records.researcher_notes: The 2016 notice from the state environmental agency says the mill runs power boilers that feed steam turbines, and that one boiler would be replaced by a gas boiler. It does not give turbine sizes. The start years of 1979 and 1982 match GEM's two units closely, which points to the same machines. The federal plant code for Fort James in GEM is 362, and the new code is 10362.

verifications.note: Georgia-Pacific Muskogee plant 10362 rows.
2016 notice for the Georgia-Pacific Muskogee mill describing power boilers feeding steam turbines.

records.plant_name: Tinker Air Force Base power station
records.question: Should the Tinker units be changed to match the federal file of 48.1 MW each for units 1 and 2 and 41 MW each for 5A and 5B?
records.finding: GEM lists units 1 and 2 together at 96 MW, operating 2026, and units 5A and 5B together at 64 MW, retired. The federal file for September 2026 lists plant 63628, Tinker, with units 1 and 2 at 48.1 MW each and units 5A and 5B at 41 MW each, out of service.

records.researcher_notes: A February 2026 story on the OG&E and Tinker Air Force Base celebration confirms the new turbines are running. The federal file still counts 5A and 5B as out of service and not expected to return, which is not the same as retired. The plant point in the federal file is the same as GEM's point.

verifications.note: Tinker plant 63628: 1 and 2 at 48.1 MW, 5A and 5B at 41 MW.
OG&E and Tinker Air Force Base celebrate new power generation, February 2026.

records.question: Is unit 4 at Grand River 426 MW as in GEM, or 594 MW as in the federal file?
records.finding: GEM gives unit 4 as 426 MW, operating from 2026. The federal file for September 2026 gives 594 MW for generator 4. The Grand River Dam Authority describes the unit as a 426 MW J-class combustion turbine dedicated on September 9.
records.recommendation: Keep 426 MW and the operating status. The federal figure of 594 MW is the old coal unit 2 size and looks like a carry-over.
records.researcher_notes: The federal file lists generator 4 as operating since September 2026, so its status agrees with GEM and disagrees with EIP, which lists the plant as under construction. The 2025 annual survey still shows unit 4 as proposed. EIP's page loads only through a script, so the page could not be read as text.

verifications.note: Grand River Dam Authority dedicates Unit 4, a 426 MW J-class turbine.
Plant 165 generator 4 at 594 MW, operating since September 2026.

records.question: Is Mustang unit 6-12 one block of 462 MW as in GEM, or seven turbines of 66 MW each as in the federal file?
records.finding: GEM lists one unit named 6-12 at 462 MW. The federal file lists seven natural gas combustion turbines, GT1 to GT7, each 66 MW, all started in 2017. Seven times 66 is 462 MW.
records.recommendation: Keep the total at 462 MW. Consider splitting the unit into seven turbines of 66 MW each.
records.researcher_notes: The totals agree. Only the way the units are counted differs.

verifications.note: Plant 2953 Mustang GT1 to GT7, 66 MW each, operating 2017.

records.question: Do federal generators 2G1, 2S1, 3G1 and 3S1 belong to GEM units CC2 and CC3?
records.finding: GEM lists CC2 and CC3 at 686.4 MW each, pre-construction, 2029. The federal file lists 2G1 at 408.8 MW and 2S1 at 277.6 MW, then 3G1 and 3S1 with the same sizes, planned for 2029 with approvals not started.
records.recommendation: Treat 2G1 and 2S1 as CC2, and 3G1 and 3S1 as CC3, since the sums of 686.4 MW agree. Consider setting the status to announced if no permit was filed.
records.researcher_notes: The federal file says regulatory approvals have not started. GEM says pre-construction. No permit filing was found in this pass.

verifications.note: Plant 8059 Comanche (OK) 2G1, 2S1, 3G1, 3S1 planned for 2029, approvals not initiated.

records.question: Are Horseshoe Lake units 10, 11 and 12 operating, as in GEM, or proposed or under construction, as other sources say?
records.finding: The federal file shows unit 10 as operating since 2001 at 60.5 MW, so EIP's proposed status for unit 10 is likely about the new units. Units 11 and 12 are listed as construction complete but not yet in commercial operation, planned for 2026. Units 13 and 14 at 224 MW each are approved but not under construction, planned for 2029.
records.recommendation: Keep unit 10 as operating and change units 11 and 12 to construction until a document shows commercial operation. Units 13 and 14 match GEM.
records.researcher_notes: A November 2025 story says the state commission approved 448 MW at Horseshoe Lake for OG&E. A status change needs two independent publishers for high confidence, and only the federal file gives the current state. Federal generator ids 13 and 14 belong to GEM units 13 and 14.

verifications.note: Plant 2951 generators 11 and 12 construction complete, not yet commercial; 13 and 14 approved, 2029.
OG&E story on approval of 448 MW of new generation at Horseshoe Lake.

records.question: Does EIP's under construction status for Anadarko describe the new Roulet units rather than the retired unit 3?
records.finding: GEM lists unit 3 as retired and units 12 and 13 as the Roulet units under construction for 2026. The federal file shows Anadarko plant units 1, 2 and 3 retired in 2024. Units 1 and 2 are 17.3 MW each and are below the threshold.
records.recommendation: Keep unit 3 as retired and the Roulet units as under construction. Treat EIP's status as describing the Roulet units.
records.researcher_notes: The EIP page loads only through a script and could not be read as text. The match between EIP's under construction status and the Roulet units is an inference.

verifications.note: Plant 3006 Anadarko units 1, 2 and 3 retired in 2024.

records.question: Is Northeastern unit 3 operating on gas as in GEM, or still coal as in the federal file?
records.finding: GEM lists unit 3 as converted to gas and operating from 2026. The federal file for September 2026 still lists generator 3 as conventional steam coal at 473 MW. Public Service Company of Oklahoma told the state in October 2025 that it would stop burning coal on December 31, 2025 and run unit 3 on gas from 2026.
records.recommendation: Keep unit 3 as operating on gas if a document confirms the conversion is done. Otherwise note the planned conversion date.
records.researcher_notes: The utility's annual report to the state environmental agency says coal burning would end at the end of 2025. It also says a required filing with the Southwest Power Pool was still pending. EIP lists this unit as proposed, which fits the new units 5 and 6 at 225 MW that GEM has as pre-construction for 2028.

verifications.note: PSO October 2025 report: stop coal at Northeastern on December 31, 2025 and run Unit 3 on gas from 2026.
Plant 2963 generator 3 still listed as conventional steam coal, 473 MW.

records.question: Should Muskogee units 4 and 5 keep the start year 2019, or change to the federal file's 1977 and 1978?
records.finding: GEM uses two rows for each unit and gives the gas conversion year of 2019 for the second row. The federal file gives 1977 and 1978 for natural gas steam turbines of 572 MW.
records.recommendation: Keep 2019 for the converted rows. The federal file shows the original start years, which GEM already holds in the first row of each unit.
records.researcher_notes: No change is needed. This follows GEM's convention for coal-to-gas conversions.

verifications.note: Plant 2952 Muskogee units 4 and 5, natural gas steam turbines, 572 MW, started 1977 and 1978.

records.question: Should Kiamichi be owned by Kiowa Power Partners alone, or by the partnerships in the federal ownership table?
records.finding: GEM lists Kiowa Power Partners LLC at 100 percent. The federal annual survey for 2025 lists Tenaska Oklahoma I LP at about 99 percent, with small shares for Tenaska Oklahoma Inc, TC Oklahoma GP and Tyr Oklahoma GP.
records.recommendation: Keep Kiowa Power Partners at 100 percent. The listed partnerships hold under five percent each apart from the main partnership, which is the Tenaska affiliate of the same owner group.
records.researcher_notes: GEM's parents, ITOCHU and Tenaska Energy, are consistent with the federal table. The entity lookup found no separate Tenaska Oklahoma entity.

verifications.note: EIA-860 page for the 2025 survey, whose owner table lists the Kiamichi shares.

records.question: Should Mooreland unit 1 be added at 45 MW?
records.finding: GEM lists units 2 and 3 at 125 and 135 MW. The federal file also lists unit 1 at 45 MW, natural gas steam turbine, from 1964.
records.recommendation: Do not add unit 1. It is below the 50 MW unit threshold.
records.researcher_notes: The plant total in the federal file is 305 MW against GEM's 260 MW. The gap is unit 1.

verifications.note: Plant 3008 Mooreland units 1, 2 and 3 at 45, 125 and 135 MW.
